questions.prompt: GTA 6's launch weekend — and the surprise is the biggest game of the year turns out to be a cozy one. Vice City's open, no rush, no score to chase. Which scene sounds most like yours tonight?

options.text: Cruising slow, radio on — the city's a place to be, not a race to win.
Main story, fully locked in — I've waited years for tonight.
A quiet corner of Vice City, just me and the sunset.
The night has its own plans — I'm just along for the ride.

questions.prompt: Five years later, Yellowjackets finally answers one of its biggest mysteries — the wait is over, the answer's right there. How are you meeting it tonight?

options.text: Straight in — I've waited five years, I'm not waiting another hour.
Savoring it slow — one episode, no rush, let it land.
Texting the group first — we waited together, we react together.
Honestly torn — half of me wants the answer, half wants the mystery back.

questions.prompt: The Blade director walked away from a Marvel movie — 'life's too short to make s**t films.' You've been pouring time into something that isn't working. Tonight, which way are you leaning?

options.text: Walking away clean — life's too short, and I feel lighter already.
One more honest shot — tonight I give it a real try, then decide.
Shelving it for now — I'll come back fresh, or I won't.
Doubling down — I can't let it go, even if it's costing me.

questions.prompt: GTA 6 turns out to be a cozy game — so tonight's session is a night in, controller in hand, nowhere to rush to. If someone handled tonight's drink for you, what would you want beside you?

options.text: A toast-worthy pour — virgin or hard, launch weekend deserves it.
Cocoa, slow sips — the controller can wait a minute.
A shareable pitcher — something for everyone in the room to pass around.
Just water, I don't need anything else tonight.

questions.prompt: Every song across all 24 radio stations in GTA VI is out there now — Vice City has a whole dial to turn. What does tonight's drive sound like to you?

options.text: Station surfing, volume up — every station's a new mood tonight.
One station locked in — letting it ride, no skipping.
The talk station — I'm here for the city's voices and the chatter.
Radio off, windows down — just the city humming underneath.

questions.prompt: Sunrise on the Reaping's opening weekend is winding down — the books are ranked, the arena's open, and the story's still buzzing. In the hour ahead, what does your evening feel like?

options.text: Straight into the story — one more chapter, one more scene, no stopping.
Easing in slow — rereading a favorite part, letting it wash over me.
Ranking the books with a friend — we've all got a different favorite.
Still deciding — too many good ways back into the story tonight.
